```shiploop-state
{
  "evidence_refs": ["original request S1", "original request S2"],
  "headline": "Intake mapped S1-S2 to 3 outcomes, scope boundaries and 5 open items, each owned by discovery or a recorded default; nothing is blocked.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "summary": "S1a (FACT from request): this is an existing Node.js project, so the work stays in this one repository and changes existing code; README.md is the author's pointer to the project docs and was not read in intake. S1b (FACT): the user store is in-memory and the HTTP server is in src/server.js, so they are the entry points and the change boundary. ASSUMPTION: both exist as named, and filtering and pagination run in-process over the store with no database, new service or new dependency. S1c (ASSUMPTION): consumers are HTTP clients and the existing tests of the user list endpoint. Risk: changing the current list response breaks them. DEFAULT: requests without the new query params keep today's behaviour and body shape. S2a (OUTCOME 1): the user list endpoint accepts a filter by name. S2b (OUTCOME 2): the same endpoint accepts pagination, a window over the results. S2c (OUTCOME 3): automated tests cover filtering and pagination, run with the project's existing test setup. S2d (BOUNDARY, no added scope): only the user list endpoint; no other endpoints, sorting, other-field filters, auth, persistence or README edits are requested. OPEN QUESTIONS: OQ1 (owner: discovery; blocks parameter names, response shape and all tests): discovery must first establish which route and method is the user list endpoint, how server.js parses query strings and writes JSON, the current response shape (array or envelope), the error style, and whether the user record has a single `name` field or first/last. OQ2 (owner: recorded default; blocks the filter semantics and their tests): DEFAULT is query param `name`, case-insensitive substring match on the user's name, and no match returns an empty list with 200. This rules out exact, fuzzy and multi-field search, and an existing README or code convention overrides it. OQ3 (owner: recorded default; blocks the pagination design and tests): DEFAULT is `limit` and `offset` params applied after filtering, in store insertion order with no sorting added. Absent params return the full list as today, and invalid values (non-integer, negative, limit 0) return 400 in the server's existing error style. This rules out cursor and page-number styles and a forced default page size, and an existing convention found by discovery wins. OQ4 (owner: recorded default; blocks only the response-shape part): DEFAULT is that the body shape is unchanged, with no total count or links added. This rules out envelope or total metadata unless discovery finds an existing envelope convention. OQ5 (owner: discovery; blocks the tests deliverable and the done-check): discovery must establish the test runner and command from package.json, where existing tests live and how they start the server (port, ephemeral). DEFAULT if none exists is Node built-in node:test with no new dependency. No person-only step exists, so nothing blocks proceeding. INTERACTION AND STATE (HTTP service): actors are, by DEFAULT, anonymous HTTP clients with no identity or auth added, and discovery checks whether server.js already identifies callers (this only matters if list results were per-caller, which the default rules out). The store is shared by all requests in one server process, and filter and page are stateless per request (DEFAULT; rules out server-side cursors or sessions). Its lifetime is until process restart (FACT from in-memory), so there is no page state to expire. Hidden: DEFAULT is that the list exposes only the fields it already exposes, with no new field hiding. The runtime provides whatever server.js uses (node http or a framework), and discovery establishes it so nothing is hand-rolled that the runtime already gives. Known limitation, accepted and not solved: store changes between page requests can shift pages. SOURCE HINTS (leads, unverified): README.md; src/server.js; the user-store module (file name unknown, probably under src/); package.json (scripts, dependencies, Node engine); the existing test directory; ambiguous terms are `name` (single field or first/last), filtering by name (exact or substring), pagination (style) and user list endpoint (which route). No team, workspace, channel, internal site, private repository or owner is named, and no sensitive locator is involved. WHERE AND WHEN VISIBLE: the target is this repository's working tree (src/server.js plus test files). The request names it, so that is the delivery grant. No release, deploy, publish or push authority is given or implied (ASSUMPTION: nothing is deployed). In an isolated run the source checkout stays at its pre-run snapshot until the final return, so the change shows there only after the final return. During the run it is visible only in the isolated working copy and its test output. At runtime the behaviour shows by starting src/server.js from the updated checkout and calling the list endpoint with the new params. No deployed target exists, so there is no release wait."
}
```
